Order 
This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed by the petitioner seeking following reliefs:-
(i) That, the impugned FIR at Crime No.256/2024 dated 19.12.2024 of Police Station Unnao, District Datia (M.P.) under section 420, 467, 468, 471/34 of IPC may kindly be directed to be quashed and set aside.
(ii) That, all consequential criminal proceedings may held to be null and void and be also quashed.
(iii) That, other relief which is just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case may also be granted.

In brief, the facts of the case are that, the petitioner was posted as Patwari at Halka No. 69, Village Guda, Tehsil and District Datia (M.P.) in the year 2019 and was also assigned charge of Halka No.
33, Village Parasari, Tehsil and District Datia (M.P.).

One Mayaram S/o Shri Puttulal submitted an application under Sections 109 and 110 of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1959 before the Court of the learned Naib Tehsildar, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4775 2 Mahadev Prasad Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62065552/
1 WP-14-2025 seeking mutation of his name in the revenue records with respect to land bearing Survey Nos. 1016, 1037, 1041, 1074, 1076, 1077 and 1085, total area admeasuring 5.99 hectares, on the basis of an alleged registered sale deed dated 04.04.2018.

sentences.text: The learned Naib Tehsildar, as per procedure, called for a report from the concerned Patwari.

In the said report, it was stated that the names of Pawan Kumar, Suryakant S/o Sitaram, Rishi Kumar, Mayank Kumar S/o Shiv Kumar and Ayush S/o Keshav Purohit were recorded as the existing owners of the aforesaid survey numbers.

After issuance of Istahar/notice inviting objections and upon no objections being received, the learned Naib Tehsildar, vide order dated 08.03.2019, allowed the mutation application and directed that the name of Mayaram S/o Puttulal be mutated in place of the earlier recorded owners.

In compliance with the order passed by the competent revenue authority, the petitioner, in his ministerial capacity as Patwari, carried out the mutation entries in accordance with the said order dated 08.03.2019.
On the basis of these revenue entries, Mayaram subsequently obtained a Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loan from Axis Bank.
Thereafter, a complaint was made by one of the previous owners, namely Mayank.

Pursuant thereto, the Collector ordered an enquiry, Consequently, the Sub-Divisional Officer, after detailed consideration of the entire record and the manner in which the order dated 08.03.2019 came to be passed, set aside the mutation order.

The petitioner was suddenly placed under suspension on 18.12.2024, and on the very next day i.e., 19.12.2024, the impugned FIR was registered against him for offences under Sections 420, 467, 466, 471 and 34 of the IPC.

Aggrieved, the petitioner had preferred the present petition on the following grounds:-
6.A

That, the impugned FIR lodged against the petitioner at Crime No.256/2024 dated 19.12.2024 of Police Station Unnao, District Datia (M.P.) is nothing but misuse of powers because the FIR and other documents does not contain the ingredients of section 420, 467, 468, 471/34 of IPC and, therefore, the impugned FIR deserves to be quashed and set aside.
6.8 That, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Bhajanlal's case has specifically ruled that the FIR is not constitute the ingredients of offence, such FIR cannot be sustained and has to be quashed.
6.C That, even otherwise the petitioner since has made compliance of a quasi-judicial order passed by his superior le.
the Court of Ld. Naib Tehsildar, no offence is made out against the petitioner, as he has acted on bonafide believe.
It is not the case of respondents that the order passed by Ld. Naib Tehsildar is forged.
It is also not the case of respondents/prosecution that the petitioner has altered the revenue entry regarding ownership of land in dispute without there being order passed by his superior.
That being so, the offence of section 420, 467, 468, 471/34 of IPC is not made out against the petitioner.
6.D That, there is no allegation with respect to pre-meeting of mind which may constitute an offence under section 34 of IPC against the petitioner and, therefore,

sentences.text: also the entire FIR deserves to be quashed and set aside.
6.E That, the other grounds shall be urged during the course of arguments.
None for the petitioner.

Learned counsel for the State submits that the impugned FIR discloses cognizable offences and a prima facie case against the petitioner, as the material collected during preliminary enquiry indicates that the mutation order was procured on the basis of a forged and fabricated sale deed and manipulated revenue record, and the petitioner, being the Patwari and custodian of land records,
actively facilitated and endorsed the illegal mutation despite existing entries showing different recorded owners.

It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4775 4 WP-14-2025 contended that the petitioner's role was not merely ministerial but involved conscious participation in the process which enabled the beneficiary to secure wrongful gain, including obtaining a Kisan Credit Card loan, thereby attracting offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 34 IPC.

The State further submits that the scope of interference under Article 226 at the stage of investigation is extremely limited, and since disputed questions of fact regarding complicity, knowledge and intention of the petitioner require thorough investigation, this is not a fit case for exercise of extraordinary jurisdiction to quash the FIR.
Hence, the petition deserves to be dismissed.
Heard learned counsel for the State at length and on perusal of the material placed on record.

By way of present petition the petitioner seeks quashment of FIR registered for offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of IPC primarily on the ground that he merely acted in compliance of an order allegedly passed by the Naib Tehsildar dated 08.03.2019 and, therefore, no criminal intent can be attributed to him; however, the reply filed by the State discloses serious and specific allegations that the mutation entries were altered by using the user ID of the petitioner.

The alleged order of the Naib Tehsildar is itself false and fabricated and not traceable in the official record or Revenue Court Management System and the petitioner failed to verify the authenticity of the said order despite being duty bound to do so, and the fraudulent entries enabled the beneficiary to obtain a Kisan Credit Card loan by mortgaging land which did not belong to him, thereby causing wrongful loss to the true owners and wrongful gain to the beneficiary.

The material NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4775 5 WP-14-2025 further shows that the SDO, upon enquiry,
found the mutation in favour of Mayaram to be fraudulent, restored the original entries and directed registration of FIR against the erring persons, and departmental proceedings culminated in termination of the petitioner from service.
At this stage, the Court cannot conduct a roving enquiry into disputed questions of fact or examine the genuineness of documents, which are matters squarely falling within the domain of investigation and trial.

The FIR, on its plain reading, discloses the essential ingredients of the alleged offences and cannot be said to be frivolous, vexatious or an abuse of the process of law so as to attract the parameters laid down in State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal reported in (1992) SCC (Cri) 426.
